skill_concept: Construct a single source file valid in two programming languages by identifying overlapping comment delimiters and string-literal syntax, using one language's comment or string construct to hide the other language's code from its parser, then iteratively compiling/interpreting both until both succeed.
verdict_reason: Both tasks require the same core procedure: identifying comment and string delimiter overlaps between two languages, using one language's syntax to hide the other's code from its parser, and iterating until both compilers/interpreters succeed. The shared procedure shape—find delimiter overlap, wrap foreign code, verify both toolchains—applies directly to both tasks.
weakest_link_reason: The Rust/C++ polyglot is significantly more complex because Rust and C++ have near-identical comment syntax with no clean string-literal escape hatch, forcing an elaborate macro-redefinition and namespace-spoofing approach that goes well beyond simple delimiter hiding.
